A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Text and visual comparisons establish only administrative and small typographic differences.

before.justification: v2 reports original latent-token intervention and probing experiments, CapImagine benchmark evaluations, and controlled ablations, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and the STARE and Hyperphantasia evaluations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same CapImagine procedure: converting intermediate visual changes into captions, refining and filtering reasoning trajectories, and training text-space imagination.

E1.justification: The training data and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including the high-resolution benchmarks, visual spatial planning analysis, BLINK, TableVQA, STARE, and Hyperphantasia.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark and intervention comparisons. Appendix C, Table 5 retains PAPO, Vision-R1, R1-Onevision, and LLaVA-OneVision.

E3.justification: The versions retain the same sampling, intervention procedures, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and training settings, including the 100-instance latent analysis and 30 derived probing questions.

E4.justification: The latent interventions and probing, rewriting/filtering/data-parity ablations, dependency analysis, efficiency comparison, and Appendix A examples are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Benchmark and intervention results retain the same point-estimate presentation, with no added or removed run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, CapImagine retains 85.9 on V* in Table 1, 70.7 overall on TableVQA in Table 2, and 40.7 overall on STARE in Table 6.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same latent-generation formulation and causal chain in Equations 1–3. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about latent-token causal disconnects and the effectiveness of CapImagine's text-space imagination.

C2.justification: The interpretations of latent degeneration and shortcut behavior are unchanged. Appendices D–E retain the qualifications concerning current LVR implementations, inference latency, and natural language's limited granularity.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is unchanged, including the project code link, data construction details, Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, eight A800-80G GPUs, batch size, and gradient accumulation.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and research positioning are unchanged. Slight spacing differences in one Wang et al. reference do not change its bibliographic content.

P1.justification: The first-page correspondence listing changes from Chi Chen and Yanghao Li to Chi Chen alone; the author list remains unchanged. The version/date text updates, while research prose and section organization remain the same.

P2.justification: The correspondence footnote reflows, the arXiv version/date stamp updates, and one reference line has slight spacing changes. All six figures and seven tables retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 changes correspondence information and minor typography while retaining the same methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and appendix qualifications. These administrative edits establish no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
